## Workspace boundary

The explicit pnpm workspace includes only these four packages. The root legacy
application sources, npm lock, dependencies, original build and tests are
retained. `build:recall` builds cache, hydration, SDK and graph core in dependency
order; `test:recall` retains the owning graph suite and actual runner-failure
verification. The new pnpm lock is resolved for this bounded workspace rather
than copied from the broad synchronization. No unrelated application, web UI,
agent package or legacy source import is selected.

The hosted verification compiles/tests the selected packages, runs the portable
recall laws and released exports, and checks actual zero-warning compiler
summaries. MiMo's own diff/stat and hygiene gates are separate from functional
execution. Prior source RED/GREEN evidence remains available in its original
bytes; freshly run checks are recorded separately.

## Codex current-head findings: persistence and identity repair

Native Codex review5479278233 inspected f5c58ebea11cc6a1e415afd371fd633884ba0658 and posted13 findings (nine P1/four P2). This actual completed finding review restores Codex availability and supersedes its historical quota observation; COMMENTED supplies no approval. The exact native review/comment JSON is retained. The initial timer test used an unavailable mock API; its original failed capture is preserved, and the corrected timer mock reproduces premature settlement against unchanged production code.

Repairs reconcile the SDK-owned TTL indexes and expiration fields on the four flat collections and existing model partitions when retention is disabled; seed both default tenant and policy only on insertion; exclude immutable tenant/storage/creation identity from update payloads; preflight finite timestamps for every batch event; and add a complete-label SHA256 digest to readable label IDs. Nested claim scopes now preserve and sort keys recursively, and unknown lifecycle actions fail closed. Absolute in-root source paths resolve directly; unsupported URL-only sources keep inline text. Single and batch vector indexing apply passage formatting only to provider inputs.

The configured embedding cache loads validated entries and atomically fsyncs/replaces its bounded snapshot at its configured path, with private temporary files and cleanup. Provider cache writes are awaited. This is restart persistence for a process-owned cache, not a distributed writer lock or a multi-process merge guarantee. The background timeout retains ownership until the original promise terminates; provider implementations without cancellation may remain pending indefinitely. It does not establish general parent/delegate fencing, bounded terminal availability, or prevent independently admitted concurrent replays.

Ordinary graph embedding rows now store `source_text_hash_sha256` from the exact untrimmed UTF8 source text. Recall admits only rows matching the current authoritative record hash; legacy unbound/stale rows return indexing-pending before query embedding/ranking. Ingest refreshes missing/changed bindings even when normalized passage text is equal. The owning writer regression includes Unicode and whitespace changes. Previously stored label/claim IDs and rows are not migrated or rewritten by this source change; deployment migration and live integration still require their own evidence.

      "body": "**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove stale vectors after replacement indexing fails**\n\nWhen an already-indexed event is replaced with new indexable text and embedding generation or storage fails, the base event has already been overwritten but this catch suppresses the error without reconciling the old hot-vector rows. Because `indexTextInMongoVectors` deletes the previous rows only after successful embedding, vector search can continue returning the removed text and metadata indefinitely, especially for retention-exempt vectors; delete or invalidate the prior parent vectors on this failure path.\n\nUseful? React with \ud83d\udc4d\u00a0/ \ud83d\udc4e.",

      "body": "**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Isolate failures while searching individual partitions**\n\nWhen a pending/error partition's cosine scan fails\u2014for example because a legacy row contains an embedding whose length does not match the partition dimension\u2014this unguarded call rejects the entire search after healthy partitions may already have produced results. Only query-embedding failures are currently recorded as unavailable, so one corrupt or unreadable partition defeats the partial-result behavior; catch execution failures per partition and report that partition as unavailable while retaining healthy hits.\n\nUseful? React with \ud83d\udc4d\u00a0/ \ud83d\udc4e.",

fails**\\n\\nWhen a lower cache layer returns a valid entry but promotion into any earlier `CacheEntryStore` rejects\\u2014for example because a writable LMDB layer is closed or out of space\\u2014the `Promise.all` rejection escapes and the layered read fails instead of returning the value that was already found. Promotion is an optimization and should be best-effort so failure of one cache layer does not make healthy lower layers unavailable.\\n\\nUseful?       "diff_hunk": "@@ -0,0 +1,145 @@\n+export interface EmbeddingCacheEntry {\n+  embedding: number[];\n+  cachedAt: number;\n+}\n+\n+import { createHash, randomUUID } from \"node:crypto\";\n+import { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\n+import { mkdir, open, rename, rm } from \"node:fs/promises\";\n+import { dirname } from \"node:path\";\n+\n+export function makeEmbeddingCacheKey(params: {\n+  model: string;\n+  text: string;\n+}): string {\n+  const digest = createHash(\"sha256\").update(params.text, \"utf8\").digest(\"hex\");\n+  return `${params.model}::${digest}`;\n+}\n+\n+export class PersistentEmbeddingCache {\n+  private map = new Map<string, number[]>();\n+  private readonly maxEntries = 10000;\n+  private flushTimer?: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;\n+  private flushQueue: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();\n+\n+  constructor(private _cachePath?: string) {\n+    if (!_cachePath) return;\n+    let saved: unknown;\n+    try { saved = JSON.parse(readFileSync(_cachePath, \"utf8\")); }\n+    catch (error) {\n+      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === \"ENOENT\") return;\n+      throw error;\n+    }\n+    if (!Array.isArray(saved)) throw new Error(\"Invalid persistent embedding cache\");\n+    for (const entry of saved) {\n+      if (!Array.isArray(entry) || entry.length !== 2 || typeof entry[0] !== \"string\"\n+        || !Array.isArray(entry[1]) || entry[1].length === 0\n+        || !entry[1].every((value: unknown) => typeof value === \"number\" && Number.isFinite(value))) {\n+        throw new Error(\"Invalid persistent embedding cache entry\");\n+      }\n+      this.map.set(entry[0], entry[1]);\n+    }\n+    this.trimToLimit();\n+  }\n+\n+  async getMany(keys: string[]): Promise<Map<string, number[]>> {\n+    const result = new Map<string, number[]>();\n+    for (const key of keys) {\n+      const entry = this.map.get(key);\n+      if (entry) {\n+        result.set(key, entry);\n+        this.map.delete(key);\n+        this.map.set(key, entry);\n+      }\n+    }\n+    return result;\n+  }\n+\n+  private trimToLimit(): void {\n+    while (this.map.size > this.maxEntries) {\n+      const firstKey = this.map.keys().next().value;\n+      if (firstKey !== undefined) this.map.delete(firstKey);\n+    }\n+  }\n+\n+  set(key: string, value: EmbeddingCacheEntry): void {\n+    this.map.delete(key);\n+    this.map.set(key, value.embedding);\n+    this.trimToLimit();\n+    this.scheduleFlush();\n+  }\n+\n+  has(key: string): boolean {\n+    return this.map.has(key);\n+  }\n+\n+  delete(key: string): void {\n+    this.map.delete(key);\n+    this.scheduleFlush();\n+  }\n+\n+  clear(): void {\n+    this.map.clear();\n+    this.scheduleFlush();\n+  }\n+\n+  get size(): number {\n+    return this.map.size;\n+  }\n+\n+  async putMany(entries: Array<{ key: string; vector: number[] }>): Promise<void> {\n+    for (const { key, vector } of entries) {\n+      this.map.delete(key);\n+      this.map.set(key, vector);\n+    }\n+    this.trimToLimit();\n+    this.scheduleFlush();\n+  }\n+\n+  private scheduleFlush(): void {\n+    if (!this._cachePath || this.flushTimer) return;\n+    this.flushTimer = setTimeout(() => {\n+      this.flushTimer = undefined;\n+      void this.flush().catch(() => console.warn(\"Embedding cache persistence failed\"));\n+    }, 5_000);\n+    this.flushTimer.unref();\n+  }",

      "diff_hunk": "@@ -0,0 +1,145 @@\n+export interface EmbeddingCacheEntry {\n+  embedding: number[];\n+  cachedAt: number;\n+}\n+\n+import { createHash, randomUUID } from \"node:crypto\";\n+import { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\n+import { mkdir, open, rename, rm } from \"node:fs/promises\";\n+import { dirname } from \"node:path\";\n+\n+export function makeEmbeddingCacheKey(params: {\n+  model: string;\n+  text: string;\n+}): string {\n+  const digest = createHash(\"sha256\").update(params.text, \"utf8\").digest(\"hex\");\n+  return `${params.model}::${digest}`;\n+}\n+\n+export class PersistentEmbeddingCache {\n+  private map = new Map<string, number[]>();\n+  private readonly maxEntries = 10000;\n+  private flushTimer?: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;\n+  private flushQueue: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();\n+\n+  constructor(private _cachePath?: string) {\n+    if (!_cachePath) return;\n+    let saved: unknown;\n+    try { saved = JSON.parse(readFileSync(_cachePath, \"utf8\"));       "diff_hunk": "@@ -0,0 +1,83 @@\n+/**\n+ * High-level SDK entry point.\n+ *\n+ * createOpenPlannerSdk() gives an internal consumer (knoxx, workers, scripts)\n+ * the full OpenPlanner data plane \u2014 event ingest, FTS/vector search, session\n+ * queries, raw mongo access \u2014 over a direct MongoDB connection with\n+ * self-sourced embeddings (EMBED_PROVIDER_*). No REST API involved: the REST\n+ * server itself is just another consumer of this library, kept for external\n+ * clients that cannot be granted database access.\n+ */\n+import { loadConfig } from \"./config.js\";\n+import type { OpenPlannerConfig } from \"./config.js\";\n+import { openMongoDB, closeMongoDB } from \"./mongodb.js\";\n+import type { MongoConnection } from \"./mongodb.js\";\n+import { createEmbeddingRuntime } from \"./embedding-runtime.js\";\n+import type { EmbeddingRuntime } from \"./embedding-runtime.js\";\n+import { createProtocols } from \"./protocol-adapters.js\";\n+import type { Protocols } from \"./protocol-adapters.js\";\n+import { ingestEvents } from \"./ingest.js\";\n+import type { IngestLogger, IngestResult } from \"./ingest.js\";\n+import { ftsSearchWithQuality, vectorSearchWithQuality } from \"./search-core.js\";\n+import type { EventEnvelopeV1, FtsSearchRequest, VectorSearchRequest } from \"./types.js\";\n+\n+export interface OpenPlannerSdkOptions {\n+  /**\n+   * Config overrides merged over loadConfig() (which reads OPENPLANNER_* /\n+   * MONGODB_* / EMBED_PROVIDER_* env vars). Pass { mongodb: { uri, ... } } to\n+   * point at a specific deployment without touching process.env.\n+   */\n+  config?: Partial<OpenPlannerConfig> & { mongodb?: Partial<OpenPlannerConfig[\"mongodb\"]> };\n+  log?: IngestLogger;\n+}\n+\n+export interface OpenPlannerSdk {\n+  config: OpenPlannerConfig;\n+  mongo: MongoConnection;\n+  embeddingRuntime: EmbeddingRuntime;\n+  protocols: Protocols;\n+  ingestEvents(events: EventEnvelopeV1[]): Promise<IngestResult>;\n+  searchFts(body: FtsSearchRequest): ReturnType<typeof ftsSearchWithQuality>;\n+  searchVector(body: VectorSearchRequest): ReturnType<typeof vectorSearchWithQuality>;\n+  listSessions(opts: { project?: string; limit: number; offset: number }): Promise<{ rows: any[]; total: number }>;\n+  getSessionEvents(sessionId: string, opts: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<any[]>;\n+  listCollections(): Promise<string[]>;\n+  close(): Promise<void>;\n+}\n+\n+export async function createOpenPlannerSdk(options: OpenPlannerSdkOptions = {}): Promise<OpenPlannerSdk> {\n+  const base = loadConfig();\n+  const config: OpenPlannerConfig = {\n+    ...base,\n+    ...(options.config ?? {}),\n+    mongodb: { ...base.mongodb, ...(options.config?.mongodb ?? {}) },\n+  };\n+\n+  const embeddingRuntime = createEmbeddingRuntime(config);\n+  const mongo = await openMongoDB(config.mongodb);\n+  let protocols: Protocols;\n+  try { protocols = createProtocols({ mongo }); }\n+  catch (error) { await closeMongoDB(mongo); throw error; }\n+  const log = options.log;\n+\n+  return {\n+    config,\n+    mongo,\n+    embeddingRuntime,\n+    protocols,\n+    ingestEvents: (events) => ingestEvents({ mongo, embeddingRuntime, log }, events),\n+    searchFts: (body) => ftsSearchWithQuality({ mongo, embeddingRuntime }, body),\n+    searchVector: (body) => vectorSearchWithQuality({ mongo, embeddingRuntime }, body),\n+    listSessions: (opts) => protocols.sessionManagement.listSessions(opts),\n+    getSessionEvents: (sessionId, opts) => protocols.sessionManagement.getSessionEvents(sessionId, opts),\n+    listCollections: async () => {\n+      const collections = await mongo.db.listCollections().toArray();\n+      return collections.map((c: { name: string }) => c.name).sort();\n+    },\n+    close: async () => {\n+      try { await embeddingRuntime.flushCaches(); }\n+      catch { console.warn(\"Embedding cache persistence failed\"); }\n+      await closeMongoDB(mongo);\n+    },",

      "body": "**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Drain background indexing before closing the SDK**\n\nWhen a caller performs `await sdk.ingestEvents(events)` and then closes the SDK without separately awaiting the returned `backgroundIndexing` promise, this closes MongoDB while the ingest-owned embedding tasks are still running. Their subsequent vector writes fail against the closed client and are swallowed by the detached `allSettled` path, leaving the admitted events permanently unindexed; the cache flush can also run before those embeddings reach the cache. Track outstanding ingest promises and await them in `close()` before flushing caches and closing MongoDB.\n\nUseful? React with \ud83d\udc4d\u00a0/ \ud83d\udc4e.",

Metrics and Kafka\n+ * publishing are intentionally NOT here \u2014 they are API-server concerns layered\n+ * on by the route.\n+ */\n+import { createHash } from \"node:crypto\";\n+import { createProtocols } from \"./protocol-adapters.js\";\n+import { upsertEvent, upsertGraphEdges, upsertGraphNodeEmbeddings } from \"./mongodb.js\";\n+import type { MongoConnection } from \"./mongodb.js\";\n+import { prepareIndexDocument } from \"./indexing.js\";\n+import { indexTextInMongoVectors, replaceMongoVectorEntries } from \"./mongo-vectors.js\";\n+import type { EventEnvelopeV1 } from \"./types.js\";\n+import { splitSentences, deduplicateByHash, computeTextHash } from \"./sentence-split.js\";\n+import { formatEmbeddingPassageText } from \"./embedding-text.js\";\n+import { eventMigrationState, OPENPLANNER_SCHEMA_TARGETS } from \"./schema-versions.js\";\n+import type { EmbeddingRuntime } from \"./embedding-runtime.js\";\n+\n+export interface IngestLogger {\n+  warn(obj: Record<string, unknown>, msg: string): void;\n+}\n+\n+export interface IngestContext {\n+  mongo: MongoConnection;\n+  embeddingRuntime: EmbeddingRuntime;\n+  log?: IngestLogger;\n+}\n+\n+export interface IngestResult {\n+  ok: true;\n+  count: number;\n+  ids: string[];\n+  projectedGraphEdges: number;\n+  ftsEnabled: true;\n+  storageBackend: \"mongodb\";\n+  indexed: true;\n+  indexing: \"queued\" | \"skipped\";\n+  queuedEventVectors: number;\n+  queuedGraphNodeEmbeddings: number;\n+  /** Events that passed validation, for downstream fan-out (e.g. Kafka). */\n+  acceptedEvents: EventEnvelopeV1[];\n+  /**\n+   * Settles when detached vector/embedding work finishes.       "body": "**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate text for every event kind**\n\nWhen an untyped JSON/JavaScript caller supplies a non-string `text` on any kind other than `graph.node`, validation accepts it; admission then stringifies it through `norm` (for example, an object becomes `\"[object Object]\"`) while `hasIndexableEventText` skips all vector and graph-node indexing. The API therefore reports the malformed event as accepted but stores corrupted text and silently omits its expected search projections. Reject non-string supplied text regardless of event kind.\n\nUseful? React with \ud83d\udc4d\u00a0/ \ud83d\udc4e.",

      "body": "**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-finite search limits before clamping**\n\nWhen an SDK caller supplies `NaN` (which is valid for the declared `number` type) or an untyped value whose numeric conversion is `NaN`, this clamp also produces `NaN`. FTS then passes it to MongoDB as a cursor limit in both the text and fallback paths, while vector search propagates the equivalent `k` value into candidate limits and can report every partition unavailable. Validate that the converted limit is finite and integral, or fall back to the default, before clamping in both search methods.\n\nUseful? React with \ud83d\udc4d\u00a0/ \ud83d\udc4e.",

      "body": "**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude caller expirations from TTL update payloads**\n\nWhen `upsertEvent` receives a typed event containing `expiresAt` while retention is disabled or the event has a retention label, spreading the event places `expiresAt` in `$set` and line 951 simultaneously places it in `$unset`. MongoDB rejects the update because the same path is modified by conflicting operators, so a valid read/modify/write of an `EventDocument` fails; `upsertCompactedMemory` has the same conflict. Remove the caller-supplied expiration before constructing the retention-controlled update.\n\nUseful? React with \ud83d\udc4d\u00a0/ \ud83d\udc4e.",

      "body": "**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize trailing slashes in the embedding base URL**\n\nWhen `EMBED_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` is configured with a normal trailing slash, this constructs a request path such as `http://provider//v1/embeddings`. Servers or proxies that do not canonicalize duplicate slashes return 404, making every embedding and vector-indexing request fail despite a valid provider URL. Strip trailing slashes from the configured base URL before appending the endpoint.\n\nUseful? React with \ud83d\udc4d\u00a0/ \ud83d\udc4e.",

      "diff_hunk": "@@ -0,0 +1,232 @@\n+/**\n+ * Protocol adapters for OpenPlanner routes.\n+ *\n+ * These adapters wrap MongoDB (or REST) operations behind protocol interfaces,\n+ * allowing routes to delegate to protocols instead of direct DB access.\n+ *\n+ * env var PROTOCOL_IMPL: \"mongo\" (default) | \"rest\"\n+ */\n+\n+import { upsertEvent, type MongoConnection } from \"./mongodb.js\";\n+\n+/**\n+ * The minimal context protocol implementations need. The REST API passes its\n+ * Fastify-decorated connection; library consumers (knoxx, workers) pass the\n+ * connection from createOpenPlannerSdk / openMongoDB directly.\n+ */\n+export interface ProtocolContext {\n+  mongo: MongoConnection;\n+}\n+\n+export interface EventAdmission {\n+  appendEvent(event: any): Promise<any>;\n+  appendEvents(events: any[]): Promise<any[]>;\n+  queryEvents(filter: any): Promise<any[]>;\n+}\n+\n+export interface SessionManagement {\n+  createSession(opts: any): Promise<any>;\n+  getSession(sessionId: string): Promise<any>;\n+  updateSession(sessionId: string, updates: any): Promise<any>;\n+  closeSession(sessionId: string): Promise<void>;\n+  listSessions(opts: { project?: string; limit: number; offset: number }): Promise<{ rows: any[]; total: number }>;\n+  getSessionEvents(sessionId: string, opts: any): Promise<any[]>;\n+}\n+\n+export interface TenantManagement {\n+  listTenants(): Promise<any[]>;\n+  getTenant(tenantId: string): Promise<any | null>;\n+  createTenant(tenant: any): Promise<any>;\n+  updateTenant(tenantId: string, updates: any): Promise<any | null>;\n+  deleteTenant(tenantId: string): Promise<boolean>;\n+  getPolicy(tenantId: string): Promise<any | null>;\n+  setPolicy(tenantId: string, policy: any): Promise<any>;\n+}\n+\n+const PROTOCOL_IMPL = process.env.PROTOCOL_IMPL ?? \"mongo\";\n+\n+// \u2500\u2500 MongoDB Implementations \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n+\n+class MongoEventAdmission implements EventAdmission {\n+  constructor(private ctx: ProtocolContext) {}\n+\n+  async appendEvent(event: any): Promise<any> {\n+    await upsertEvent(this.ctx.mongo.events, event, this.ctx.mongo.retention?.eventsTtlSeconds);\n+    return event;\n+  }\n+\n+  async appendEvents(events: any[]): Promise<any[]> {\n+    for (const event of events) await this.appendEvent(event);\n+    return events;\n+  }\n+\n+  async queryEvents(filter: any): Promise<any[]> {\n+    return this.ctx.mongo.events.find(filter).sort({ ts: -1 }).toArray();\n+  }\n+}\n+\n+class MongoSessionManagement implements SessionManagement {\n+  constructor(private ctx: ProtocolContext) {}\n+\n+  async createSession(opts: any): Promise<any> {\n+    const doc = { ...opts, kind: \"session\", createdAt: new Date(), updatedAt: new Date() };\n+    await this.ctx.mongo.events.insertOne(doc);\n+    return doc;",

      "body": "**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply event retention when creating session rows**\n\nWhen event retention is enabled, `createSession` inserts directly into the events collection without setting `expiresAt` or using `upsertEvent`. The SDK's absolute TTL index only examines `expiresAt`, so session rows\u2014including any metadata in `opts`\u2014remain indefinitely even after ordinary events expire; this also differs from legacy relative TTL indexes because the row does have `createdAt`. Create the session through the retention-aware writer or assign the configured absolute expiry.\n\nUseful? React with \ud83d\udc4d\u00a0/ \ud83d\udc4e.",

      "diff_hunk": "@@ -0,0 +1,807 @@\n+/**\n+ * Event ingest pipeline, extracted from the REST API's POST /v1/events handler\n+ * so it can run in-process anywhere the SDK is embedded (the API server is one\n+ * consumer; knoxx's direct-mongo client is another). Metrics and Kafka\n+ * publishing are intentionally NOT here \u2014 they are API-server concerns layered\n+ * on by the route.\n+ */\n+import { createHash } from \"node:crypto\";\n+import { createProtocols } from \"./protocol-adapters.js\";\n+import { upsertEvent, upsertGraphEdges, upsertGraphNodeEmbeddings } from \"./mongodb.js\";\n+import type { MongoConnection } from \"./mongodb.js\";\n+import { prepareIndexDocument } from \"./indexing.js\";\n+import { indexTextInMongoVectors, replaceMongoVectorEntries } from \"./mongo-vectors.js\";\n+import type { EventEnvelopeV1 } from \"./types.js\";\n+import { splitSentences, deduplicateByHash, computeTextHash } from \"./sentence-split.js\";\n+import { formatEmbeddingPassageText } from \"./embedding-text.js\";\n+import { eventMigrationState, OPENPLANNER_SCHEMA_TARGETS } from \"./schema-versions.js\";\n+import type { EmbeddingRuntime } from \"./embedding-runtime.js\";\n+\n+export interface IngestLogger {\n+  warn(obj: Record<string, unknown>, msg: string): void;\n+}\n+\n+export interface IngestContext {\n+  mongo: MongoConnection;\n+  embeddingRuntime: EmbeddingRuntime;\n+  log?: IngestLogger;\n+}\n+\n+export interface IngestResult {\n+  ok: true;\n+  count: number;\n+  ids: string[];\n+  projectedGraphEdges: number;\n+  ftsEnabled: true;\n+  storageBackend: \"mongodb\";\n+  indexed: true;\n+  indexing: \"queued\" | \"skipped\";\n+  queuedEventVectors: number;\n+  queuedGraphNodeEmbeddings: number;\n+  /** Events that passed validation, for downstream fan-out (e.g. Kafka). */\n+  acceptedEvents: EventEnvelopeV1[];\n+  /**\n+   * Settles when detached vector/embedding work finishes. Callers that need\n+   * read-your-writes (tests, batch jobs) can await it; the API route does not.\n+   */\n+  backgroundIndexing: Promise<void>;\n+}\n+\n+function norm(v: any): string | null {\n+  if (v === undefined || v === null) return null;\n+  return String(v);\n+}\n+\n+export function validateEvent(ev: EventEnvelopeV1) {\n+  if (!ev || ev.schema !== \"openplanner.event.v1\") throw new Error(\"event.schema must be openplanner.event.v1\");\n+  for (const field of [\"id\", \"source\", \"kind\"] as const) {\n+    if (typeof ev[field] !== \"string\" || !ev[field].trim()) {\n+      throw new Error(`event.${field} must be a nonblank string`);\n+    }\n+  }\n+  if (typeof ev.ts !== \"string\" || !ev.ts.trim() || !Number.isFinite(Date.parse(ev.ts))) throw new Error(\"event.ts must be a valid timestamp (ISO)\");\n+  if (ev.kind === \"graph.node\" && ev.text !== undefined && typeof ev.text !== \"string\") {\n+    throw new Error(\"graph.node event text must be a string when supplied\");\n+  }\n+}\n+\n+function hasIndexableEventText(ev: EventEnvelopeV1): boolean {\n+  return typeof ev.text === \"string\" && ev.text.trim().length > 0;\n+}\n+\n+function labelSlug(value: string): string {\n+  return value.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, \"-\").replace(/^-+|-+$/g, \"\").slice(0, 96) || \"label\";\n+}\n+\n+function graphLabelId(tenantId: string, label: string): string {\n+  return `label:${tenantId}:${labelSlug(label)}:${createHash(\"sha256\").update(label, \"utf8\").digest(\"hex\")}`;\n+}\n+\n+function eventLabels(extra: Record<string, unknown>): string[] {\n+  const labels = (extra.openplanner_labels as any)?.labels;\n+  if (!Array.isArray(labels)) return [];\n+  return [...new Set(labels.map((label) => String(label ?? \"\").trim()).filter(Boolean))];\n+}\n+\n+export function shouldIndexEventHotVectors(ev: EventEnvelopeV1): boolean {\n+  if (!hasIndexableEventText(ev)) return false;\n+\n+  // graph.node receives dedicated node-embedding materialization below, and\n+  // graph.edge text is mostly structural glue (e.g. mentions_web URLs). Running\n+  // both through the generic hot vector path just burns response time and can\n+  // hold /v1/events open long enough for upstream header timeouts.\n+  if (ev.kind === \"graph.node\" || ev.kind === \"graph.edge\") return false;\n+\n+  return true;\n+}\n+\n+async function withTimeout<T>(promise: Promise<T>, timeoutMs: number, label: string): Promise<T> {\n+  let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;\n+  let timedOut = false;\n+  try {\n+    return await Promise.race([\n+      promise,\n+      new Promise<T>((_resolve, reject) => {\n+        timer = setTimeout(() => { timedOut = true; reject(new Error(`${label} timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms`)); }, timeoutMs);\n+      }),\n+    ]);\n+  } catch (error) {\n+    if (timedOut) {\n+      // Provider cancellation is not available on every embedding implementation.\n+      // Retain ownership until the underlying operation settles; expiry is not termination.\n+      try { await promise; } catch { /* Preserve the original timeout outcome. */ }\n+    }\n+    throw error;\n+  } finally {\n+    if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);\n+  }\n+}\n+\n+const noopLogger: IngestLogger = { warn: () => {} };\n+\n+// SDK connection-local ownership. A replacement waits for earlier detached\n+// writes to terminate; this is not a distributed writer or fencing protocol.\n+const ingestTails = new WeakMap<MongoConnection, Map<string, Promise<void>>>();\n+\n+export async function ingestEvents(ctx: IngestContext, events: EventEnvelopeV1[]): Promise<IngestResult> {\n+  const unique = new Map<string, EventEnvelopeV1>();\n+  const payloads = new Map<string, string>();\n+  for (const event of events) {\n+    validateEvent(event);\n+    const payload = JSON.stringify(event);\n+    const previous = payloads.get(event.id);\n+    if (previous !== undefined && previous !== payload) {\n+      throw new Error(`conflicting event replacements in one batch: ${event.id}`);\n+    }\n+    payloads.set(event.id, payload);\n+    unique.set(event.id, event);\n+  }\n+  const tails = ingestTails.get(ctx.mongo) ?? new Map<string, Promise<void>>();\n+  ingestTails.set(ctx.mongo, tails);\n+  const predecessors = [...unique.keys()].map(id => tails.get(id)).filter((tail): tail is Promise<void> => tail !== undefined);\n+  let complete!: () => void;\n+  const terminal = new Promise<void>(resolve => { complete = resolve; });\n+  // Reserve the complete batch without yielding, avoiding overlapping-batch\n+  // lock ordering. Refuse replacement\n+  // rather than mutate the event and retain stale or delete another owner.\n+  for (const ev of events) {\n+    const previous = await mongo.events.findOne({ _id: ev.id });\n+    if (previous?.kind === \"graph.edge\") {\n+      const old = (previous.extra as Record<string, unknown> | undefined) ?? {};\n+      const source = norm(old.source_node_id)?.trim();\n+      const target = norm(old.target_node_id)?.trim();\n+      const kind = (norm(old.edge_type) ?? norm(old.edge_kind))?.trim();\n+      if (source && target && kind) {\n+        const legacy = await mongo.graphEdges.findOne({ _id: `${source}||${target}||${kind}` });\n+        if (legacy && legacy.data?.source_event_id !== ev.id) {\n+          throw new Error(`graph projection ownership unavailable for event ${ev.id}`);\n+        }\n+      }\n+    }\n+  }\n+\n+  const ids: string[] = [];\n+  const acceptedEvents: EventEnvelopeV1[] = [];\n+  const eventVectorTasks: Array<() => chunk_count: number;\n+  }>();\n+  const sourceExpiries = new Map<string, Date | null>();\n+\n+  const derivedGraphNodeOps = new Map<string, any>();\n+  const graphLabelNodeOps: any[] = [];\n+  const queuedGraphLabelIds = new Set<string>();\n+  const now = new Date();\n+\n+  const queueDerivedGraphNodeEvent = (params: {\n+    id: string;\n+    ts: Date;\n+    project?: string | null;\n+    nodeId: string;\n+    nodeKind: string;\n+    label: string;\n+    preview: string;\n+    retentionLabels: string[];\n+    sourceEventId: string;\n+    extra?: Record<string, unknown>;\n+  }): void => {\n+    derivedGraphNodeOps.set(params.id, {\n+      updateOne: {\n+        filter: { _id: params.id },\n+        update: {\n+          $set: {\n+            id: params.id,\n+            ts: params.ts,\n+  role: null,\n+            author: null,\n+            model: null,\n+            tags: null,\n+            text: \"\",\n+            attachments: null,\n+            extra: {\n+              ...(params.extra ?? {}),\n+              node_id: params.nodeId,\n+              node_kind: params.nodeKind,\n+              label: params.label,\n+              preview: params.preview,\n+ schema_version: OPENPLANNER_SCHEMA_TARGETS.event,\n+            migration_state: eventMigrationState(now),\n+            updatedAt: now,\n+          },\n+          $setOnInsert: {\n+            createdAt: now,\n+          },\n+        },\n+        upsert: true,\n+      },\n+    });\n+  };\n+\n+  const queueNodeEmbedding = (params: {\n+    nodeId: string;\n+    sourceEventId: string;\n+ \"site_admin\": false\n      },\n      \"body\": \"**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Drain background indexing before closing the SDK**\\n\\nWhen a caller performs `await sdk.ingestEvents(events)` and then closes the SDK without separately awaiting the returned `backgroundIndexing` promise, this closes MongoDB while the ingest-owned embedding tasks are still running.
